chunks: And from him, from Abu al-Hasan al-Nakha'i, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Regarding the residents of the Sacred Mosque (Ahl al-Haram), he said: 'That which is below the Miqat (stations of consecration) up to Mecca is the residence of the Sacred Mosque, and they do not have the right to perform Tamattu' (the type of Hajj combining Umrah and Hajj). And whoever leaves Mecca to one of the provinces (cities) and then returns to it, reaching one of the Miqat stations, then there is no harm in him performing Tamattu'. This was narrated.'

key_terms.حَاضِرِي الْمَسْجِدِ الْحَرَامِ: Residents of the Sacred Mosque (Ahl al-Haram)
key_terms.مُتْعَةٌ: Tamattu' (a type of Hajj combining Umrah and Hajj)

ai.seo_question: Do residents of Mecca perform Tamattu' Hajj or Qiran?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the legal status of Mecca's residents (Ahl al-Haram) regarding the Tamattu' Hajj, establishing that their residence within the Miqat boundaries precludes them from performing the Umrah-Hajj combination typical of non-residents. It further introduces a nuanced exception: if a resident travels to a neighboring province and returns via a Miqat, they temporarily regain the non-resident status, allowing them to perform Tamattu'. This ruling highlights the dynamic nature of Hajj jurisprudence in Shia tradition, where geographical movement can alter ritual obligations.
